findings.reason: a coordinator following the skill as written either loops or loses the queue place the same caveat exists to preserve, and the fix is one clause naming the local lane or the in-place re-route verb.
findings.text: the caveat says a metered-lane request still `awaiting-upstream` or `queued` after its upstream lands "is discarded and dispatched again", but the re-dispatch names no lane, so the picker can pick the same metered lane and the new request stalls again (`admit_once` receives `lane` from `reckon crew admit --lane clive`, the deployed fleet service in `~/.config/fleet/services.json`, and skips every pointer whose backend differs); `crew queue edit --backend` from §5 re-routes the queued request in place, and `crew queue drop` withdraws it without the place loss `crew discard` causes

response_events.reason: the re-dispatch happens after the upstream has landed, so the request is ready; a ready request routed to a metered lane launches at dispatch (that lane has no admission queue) or is refused with budget-hold, so it cannot park on a metered lane again
